title: Flatness survives restriction to a slice
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a flat $\mathcal O$-module [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Then the restriction $\mathcal F|_U$ is a flat $\mathcal O_U$-module on the slice site over $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

proof.text: Tensoring by the restricted flat sheaf preserves finite limits by the slice finite-limit lemma.
The closed monoidal structure makes tensorLeft a left adjoint. Symmetry identifies tensorRight with tensorLeft, so tensorRight preserves finite colimits.
Combine finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation using exactFunctor_iff. By the definition of flatness, the restricted sheaf is flat.
